solves: Holds the place of a content whose shape is known while it loads, with a still shape that does not move the layout when the content arrives.
use_when: When the shape of the content is known and it is still loading.
Choose the shape equal to the content: line for text, block for an image or area, avatar for a person.
Repeat the shape of the final content, because the swap must not move the layout.
Use the avatar shape in the size of the nph-avatar that will come in, because the size stays the same.
Announce the wait on the container, because the shape is not read.
Keep the piece still, because it has no pulse.
do_not_use_when: When the shape of the content is not known: use nph-spinner.
When there is no content, or as an empty state: use nph-empty.
One avatar size in place of another: use the avatar shape of the same size.

shape.constraint: Reflects because the internal CSS selects the box by it. It is the Figma property forma. A value outside the list draws nothing and emits console.error in development.

shape.choose_when: line for text, block for an image, chart or area, avatar-sm, avatar-md or avatar-lg for an nph-avatar of the same size.

default.changes_for_user: A still rectangle holds the place of the content; it does not change with interaction.

business_rules: The shape always uses color/muted, with no border, no text and no animation: it carries no state.
The line takes its own skeleton/line-height; the space between lines comes from whoever uses it.
The line and the block stretch to the container width. The block height follows the content that will come in, so whoever uses it gives the height.
The avatar takes avatar/size-* and avatar/radius-*, like nph-avatar, with rounded corners and never a circle.
The wait is announced by the container with aria-busy, not by the piece.
ai_hints: Use nph-skeleton when the shape of the content is known and it is loading; when the shape is not known, use nph-spinner.
Use nph-skeleton for the place of content that will come in; when there is no content, use nph-empty.
Choose the shape equal to the content: line for text, block for an image or area, avatar-sm, avatar-md or avatar-lg for a person in the size of the nph-avatar that will come in.
Put aria-busy on the loading container, because nph-skeleton is decorative and is not read.

accessibility.semantics: The host is `aria-hidden`: the shape is decorative and stays out of the accessibility tree. The loading container gets `aria-busy` while it waits.
accessibility.focus: The piece does not receive focus.
accessibility.contrast: The shape carries no information: the contrast with the background is low on purpose and does not need to reach 3:1.
accessibility.color_alternative: The wait is announced by the container, not by the color of the shape. The piece is still, so there is no pulse to reduce under reduced motion.

invalid_combinations: One avatar size in place of another — the size would change when the content arrives.
Text inside the shape — the shape holds no text.
Another color or an animation — the shape always uses color/muted and is still.
anti_patterns: Using the skeleton as an empty state.
Using the skeleton when the shape of the content is not known.
Using one avatar size in place of another.
Animating the shape or painting it with another color.

sources.design_md: design.md, color/muted, skeleton/line-height, radius/inner, radius/control, avatar/size-* and avatar/radius-*
sources.decision: P69 — API and semantics of nph-skeleton, 15-10-2026
sources.usage_evidence: none in code yet; the accepted frame shows a list of people, a card and a paragraph loading
